answer.generated: The compressed instruction format (RV32IC) in RISC-V reduces the instruction word size to 16 bits, allowing common intermediate instructions with small values and simple ALU operations to be encoded efficiently. This differs from the standard three-address format used in traditional RISC computers, which typically uses 32-bit instructions. By using shorter instructions, RV32IC improves code density and potentially increases throughput in pipelined processors, though it may limit flexibility for complex operations that require more than two operands.
